title: Prospective, randomized, controlled, multicenter, operative study to evaluate the role of intraoperative sonography compared to the preoperative wire localization in the treatment of non-palpable breast cancer
summary:
Typically for breast-sparing surgical removal of a non-palpable breast tumor is a marker of the tumor before or during surgery an important prerequisite for the surgeon to remove the "right" tissue. Standard is still a marker for the removed position by means of a wire. The wire marker is usually just before surgery. Thus, the wire is placed in the right place, carried the mark using a mammography or ultrasound guidance. After surgery, the removed tissue with the wire is sent again to a mammography or ultrasound guidance. So, it is possible to say with a relatively high probability whether the tumor is completely removed or a further excision of tissue is required. This control is carried out while the patient still is under anesthesia.
A relatively new method for localization of non-palpable tumor represents the ultrasound examination. In this method, the operation is carried out under "ultrasound image". The surgeon can identify with the help of ultrasound the tumor. The position of the tumor is marked on the skin. The surgeon may use ultrasound examination at any time during operation in order to determine the necessary extent of the surgery. The goal is still to remove the tumor together with healthy tissue, without removing an unnecessary amount of tissue.Which method for the application is carried out by means of random allocation (randomization).
In this study, an answer to the question is to be found, whether the ultrasound method is equivalent to the standard wire method.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- written consent after verbal clarification by an
Study physician for this study is available
- Histologically proven invasive breast cancer
- Non-palpable tumor
- Indication for BEI
- CT1b-cT2
- Female patient> 18 years
- Sonographically detectable tumor in two levels
- Karnofsky Performance Status - Index ≥70% or ECOG <2
Exclusion criteria:
- Multifocal tumor
- Recurrence of breast cancer
- Tumor <5mm
- Inability to understand the meaning and purpose of the clinical trial or the comply with conditions for studying
